title: Velo3D Selected for U.S. Defense Award with Potential Value of Up to $10 Million for UAS Warhead and Lethal Payload Systems
body_markdown:
**Program will use advanced metal additive manufacturing to support U.S. defense production**


FREMONT, Calif.


, Nov. 16, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Velo3D, Inc. (Nasdaq: VELO), a leader in advanced metal additive manufacturing technology, today announced it has been selected for an award under the Low-Cost Warheads and Lethal Payloads for Unmanned Systems challenge. The award has a potential total value of up to $10 million, subject to the Government's future funding of subsequent program phases.


Velo3D was selected by DEVCOM Armaments Center through the ONIX Marketplace, operated by One Nation Innovation (ONI), under an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) acquisition pathway designed to accelerate the transition of commercial technologies into defense applications.


Under the program, Velo3D will establish and operationally validate modular payload architectures, scalable manufacturing approaches, advanced warhead components, rapid manufacturability, and supply-chain resilience. The effort will focus on two material pathways: Inconel 718 and a second, Government-directed high-performance alloy. Velo3D will be responsible for additive manufacturing process development, production, inspection and quality documentation. The Government will retain design authority and responsibility for lethality, ballistic, functional and performance testing.


"This award demonstrates the role advanced manufacturing can play in strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base," said Arun Jeldi, CEO of Velo3D. "Our technology and manufacturing expertise can help the Government evaluate new materials, produce complex components and establish repeatable production processes for critical defense applications."


The program will use laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing to produce components that can be difficult or uneconomical to manufacture using conventional methods. The effort will progress through process development, initial hardware production, Government testing and refinement, followed by a low-rate initial production demonstration.


"Velo3D's technology and scale hold a lot of promise for bringing new capabilities to the Warfighter," said Dan Suarez, Research Engineer, U.S. Army DEVCOM Armaments Center.


Velo3D's Inconel 718 process is qualified on its Sapphire® platform, providing an established manufacturing baseline for one material pathway. The second pathway will develop and qualify the additive manufacturing process for a second, Government-directed high-performance alloy.


The program also includes development of a Technology Transition Package documenting manufacturing processes, quality requirements and production procedures. The package will support repeatable production at qualified domestic manufacturing facilities.


The award expands Velo3D's work with the U.S. Department of Defense and its role in supporting mission-critical defense manufacturing.


**About Velo3D**


Velo3D is a metal 3D printing technology company that enables customers to build mission-critical metal parts. The fully integrated solution includes the Flow™ print preparation software, the Sapphire® family of printers and the Assure™ quality control system — all powered by Velo3D's Intelligent Fusion® manufacturing process. Learn more at[velo3d.com](https://www.velo3d.com/) .
